newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Nicaraguan president seeks Taiwan investment.
newsitem.headline: Nicaraguan president seeks Taiwan investment.

text.p: Visiting Nicaraguan President Arnoldo Aleman on Thursday sought Taiwan investment, saying his country is full of opportunities.

"Nicaragua is filled with enticement of investment. I believe Taiwan enterprises can find unlimited trade opportunities and development areas," the state-funded Central News Agency quoted Aleman as saying.
Aleman said hardworking and honest Nicaraguan people were his country's biggest asset, and the rapid economic growth in Nicaragua has ensured steady gains for investors.
Nicaragua's economic growth rate stood at 5.5 percent in 1996, and was expected to increase to seven percent at the end of 1997, Aleman said.
Aleman arrived in Taiwan on Tuesday for a five-day state visit.
Taiwan, which rolled out the red carpet for Aleman's visit, has promised economic aid for Nicaragua, which is among only 30 nations that recognise Taipei instead of its rival Beijing.
Nicaraguan visiting Foreign Minister Emilio Alvarez on Wednesday asked Taiwan to help develop a port project.
Aleman's visit will be closely followed by a similar visit by Costa Rican President Jose Maria Figueres, who was expected to arrive in Taiwan on Saturday.

Central American nations have courted Taiwan as a needed source of foreign investment, and Taiwan in turn has welcomed their diplomatic support amid growing efforts by Beijing to isolate it internationally.
Costa Rica, Nicaragua and a handful of other countries recently proposed a discussion on granting Taiwan U.N. membership during a General Assembly session in September.
Beijing took over China's U.N. seat in 1971 when Taiwan, to which the Nationalist Chinese government retreated in 1949 following a civil war, was expelled from the United Nations.
China regards the island as a renegade province and reacts fiercely to any move to recognise or seat Taiwan.
